thread.title: Apple snags ‘Parenthood’ showrunner for streaming

author: Annlee Ellingson
title: Apple snags ‘Parenthood’ showrunner for streaming
text: Jan 17, 2019, 11:58am PST Streaming has lured another high-profile showrunner away from traditional television. This time it’s Apple Inc. signing Jason Katims and his True Jack Productions to an exclusive multi-year overall deal for its forthcoming video platform. Katims has created such TV shows as “Parenthood” and “Roswell” and executive produced “Friday Night Lights” and “The Path.” He’ll move over to Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) this summer when his contract with Universal TV is up. At Apple he’ll reunite with Michelle Lee, who previously served as head of development at True Jack and now is on Apple’s creative development team. Her replacement at True Jack, Jeni Mulein, will also be moving to Apple. Katims also follows Kerry Ehrin, his former colleague on “Parenthood" and “Friday Night Lights,” among other projects who’s now working on Apple’s morning show drama starring Reese Witherspoon and Jennifer Aniston. After moving to Apple, Katims will stay involved with a couple of projects he set up while at Universal TV, including “Away,” a space drama ordered straight to series by Netflix, and “Sisters” for Fox. He is just the latest showrunner to move to streaming, following the moves of Ryan Murphy (“American Horror Story”), Shonda Rhimes (“How to Get Away With Murder”) and Kenya Barris (“black-ish”) to Netflix. Meanwhile, Apple has inked deals with Justin Lin (several “Fast & Furious” movies and “Star Trek: Beyond”), Oprah Winfrey, the Sesame Workshop and the Peanuts brand. Katims is represented by CAA and attorney Ira Schreck.
